articles.title: Will Sara Duterte, Mayor Baste appear at the impeachment trial? It depends, says the VP
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte was mum on whether or not she and her brother Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte will attend her impeachment trial.

blocks.text: Published September 25, 2026 7:28pm
Vice President Sara Duterte was mum on whether or not she and her brother Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte will attend her impeachment trial.

The impeachment court has already issued a subpoena to Baste Duterte, while the House prosecution panel has expressed its intent to have Sara Duterte summoned to answer the charges lodged against her.
“Anong ibig sabihin? Manood ako doon sa kanilang sarsuela? Well, depende, wala pa namang pagpapatawag sa akin,” Sara Duterte said in an ambush interview in Davao City.
(What do you mean? That I will go there and watch their dance? Well, it depends, no one has called me yet.)
The vice president also said that she was already represented by her lawyers in the trial.
“Ang impeachment ay isang legal na process at yung pagpunta ng aking mga abogado doon, yun ang aking appearance at participation doon sa proseso na yun,” she said.
(The impeachment is a legal process and my lawyers are already there and that is already my appearance and participation in that process.)
Sara Duterte was also uncertain whether her brother Baste Duterte would attend.
“Wala akong info kung a-attend siya, pero ang napag-usapan namin noon at that time, mayroong subpoena sa kanya so sinabihan ko siya bago pa man lumabas,” she said.
(I do not have info if he will attend, but when we talked about it at the time, there was a subpoena against him and I told him before it came out.)
Baste Duterte will consult the city legal office, according to the vice president.
Asked about the overturning of the decision that set the conviction threshold at 16, Sara Duterte declined to comment, saying that her lawyers might scold her.
Bags of cash?

During the ambush interview, Duterte was also asked about an allegation that she received a large amount of cash that was delivered to her family. The question, coming from a person who did not disclose her media outlet, traced the allegation to Palace Press Officer Claire Castro.
Sara Duterte said that she has not seen any such report, but proceeded to lambast Castro anyway.

“Hindi ko napanood, yung sinabi niya so hindi ako maka-comment but coming from Claire Castro, alam naman natin na isa siya kahihiyan sa ating bansa so sabi ko nga lagi sa media, wag niyo bigyan ng espasyo yung mga ganyan,” she said.
(I did not watch what she said so I could not comment but coming from Claire Castro, we know that she is a shame to our country so I always tell the media, do not give those things space.)
GMA News Online has already sought clarification from Castro regarding the matter and will update the story once she responds. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Tour Montparnasse renovation halted amid disagreements between owners
articles.summary:
Plans to modernise ‘Paris’s ugliest building’ at a standstill after clashes over plans and pricing

It has been called a carbuncle on the Paris skyline, a sombre skyscraper where visitors to…

blocks.text: It has been called a carbuncle on the Paris skyline, a sombre skyscraper where visitors to its viewing platform often joke that the city looks better when you can’t see the building itself.

The much-maligned Tour Montparnasse, a lone, dark monolith with tinted windows rising above a historic neighbourhood in the south of the city, is once again at the centre of controversy after its long-awaited renovation was halted this week because of disagreements between its many private co-owners.
The tower, which opened in 1973, is the tallest skyscraper in inner-city Paris and is also considered its ugliest building.

blocks.caption: Paris’s tallest inner-city skyscraper is due to undergo a massive structural transition. Photograph: Frédéric Vielcanet/Alamy

blocks.text: For more than a decade, plans have been thrashed out to overhaul the building and brighten its looming presence and modernise the area around it. Architects had planned to entirely refit the 210-metre structure with a new glass exterior, adding vegetation throughout, with a garden terrace on the 16th floor and an agricultural greenhouse at the top. The plans included a hotel on three floors of the 59-storey building, as well as new office and leisure spaces.
But alongside a significant operation to remove asbestos, the estimated price of the project more than doubled to €800m (£688m).

The building’s private co-owners, which include French investment funds and insurers, met this week for a final vote on the start of a first phase of renovation, with asbestos removal, interior stripping and a partial facade removal. After clashes over plans and pricing, more than three-quarters of the co-owners voted against the project.

It was the last opportunity to launch the project before the building permit granted for the tower’s renovation expires at the end of November. There are now concerns that the building, which has been emptied and closed for renovation, will loom deserted. This summer, fire officers intervened after bits of glass fell off the building and landed on the street below, although no one was hurt.

blocks.caption: Opposition councillors on the left have suggested the ‘obsolete’ tower should come down. Photograph: Bim/Getty Images

blocks.text: “Everyone needs to come to their senses,” said Philippe Goujon, the rightwing mayor of Paris’s 15th district where the tower is located. He told Agence France-Presse: “I cannot accept seeing a project that took 10 years to develop thrown away, or allowing this world-renowned landmark to fall into neglect.”

Four of the co-owners who still want a renovation, including the tycoon Xavier Niel, said in a joint statement: “We would like all the co-owners, financial partners and public authorities to meet soon to examine all the solutions to transform the Montparnasse Tower.”
Some co-owners hope that a new, scaled-down project could be agreed upon.

blocks.caption: Many commercial spaces within the tower have been left derelict. Photograph: Abaca Press/Alamy

blocks.text: Separately, the architect Renzo Piano has been tasked with overhauling the shopping centre beneath the tower and other buildings nearby, opening up new pedestrian spaces and moving from grey concrete to a greener, planted space. Local officials want to avoid delays to that project if the tower’s renovation stalls.
The office of the Socialist mayor of Paris, Emmanuel Grégoire, said it wanted “an alternative solution to be proposed” so the site does not stay at a standstill.
Opposition councillors on the left have suggested the “obsolete” tower should instead come down and be replaced by a park that would have a cooling effect during summer heatwaves.

articles.title: 'Ayoko na rin pong andito ako': Vince Dizon asked about lapsed appointment as DPWH chief
articles.summary: Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon was questioned on Friday about his lapsed appointment as department chief, which was supposed to end on September 1, 2026,…

blocks.text: Published September 25, 2026 7:08pm

Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon was questioned on Friday about his lapsed appointment as department chief, which was supposed to end on September 1, 2026, according to Senator Imee Marcos.
In response, the DPWH chief said he would be more than happy to leave the post if it is declared that his tenure has already ended, adding that the job was extremely challenging.
"Permission to speak frankly. Ma'am, this is music to my ears kasi medyo ayoko na rin pong nandito ako eh, so gusto ko na pong wala ako dito. Okay na po ito, masaya pa po ako," Dizon said.

(Permission to speak frankly. Ma'am, this is music to my ears because I also somewhat don't want to be here anymore, so I would really prefer not to be here. This is fine with me, and I would even be happy about it.)

"To be quite frank, it would be very welcome kung totoo po 'yung sinasabi ninyo na hindi na ako secretary ng DPWH. I will be more than happy to accept that kasi napakahirap po ng trabaho na to," he added.

(To be quite frank, it would be very welcome if what you're saying is true—that I am no longer the secretary of the DPWH. I will be more than happy to accept that because this job is extremely difficult.)
Marcos raised the issue after she followed up with Dizon a letter of inquiry she sent to his office on September 2.
The senator said she did not receive any reply from the secretary within seven days, pursuant to their administrative code.
"I'm sorry, but the Administrative Code is very clear that it is only one year, and if you are appointed in an acting capacity, September 1, 2025, it has lapsed in 2026," Marcos asked Dizon.
"Today is [September] 25, 2026—overdue na po kayo ng ilang araw. What is the present status, therefore, of your appointment?" she added.
(Today is [September] 25, 2026—you are overdue by several days. What is the present status, therefore, of your appointment?)
Dizon said that he has yet to confer with the Office of the President to clarify the status of his appointment.
Citing information from DPWH Chief-of-Staff Undersecretary Ricardo Bernabe III, Dizon pointed out that his appointment continues until the session of Congress ends and goes into recess.
"Usec. Bernabe just told me that… my appointment po as the Secretary is continuing until the session of Congress ends and in recess. After which I need to be reappointed," Dizon said.
Dizon took his oath as DPWH chief on September 1, 2025, replacing former secretary Manuel Bonoan, who resigned from the post amid public pressure over the flood control scandal.

Dizon was serving as the Department of Transportation secretary at the time, but his stint was cut short to conduct a "full organizational sweep" within the DPWH as ordered by President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr.
According to Dizon, in the past year, at least 61 DPWH employees found to have ties to anomalies were removed from office, with some facing pending charges.
Meanwhile, at least 19 contractors have been referred to the Office of the Ombudsman, and 11 contractors have been blacklisted, the DPWH chief added. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Batas na nag-uurong sa Brgy. at SK elections upang gawin sa Nov. 2028, pirmado na ni Marcos
articles.summary: Pinirmahan na ni Pangulong Ferdinand Marcos Jr. ang bagong batas para ipagpaliban ang nakatakdang Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE) sa darating na Nobyembre, upang iusog sa Nobyembre…

blocks.text: Pinirmahan na ni Pangulong Ferdinand Marcos Jr. ang bagong batas para ipagpaliban ang nakatakdang Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE) sa darating na Nobyembre, upang iusog sa Nobyembre 2028. Ang termino ng mga opisyal ng barangay, pinapahaba rin ng limang taon.

"Sa paglagda natin sa Republic Act No, 12326, na nagtatakda ng limang taong termino para sa mga opisyal ng barangay at Sangguniang Kabataan, malinaw ang ating inaasahan sa ating mga kasalukuyang opisyal. Gamitin ang panahong ito upang mas pagbutihin ang serbisyo, tapusin ang mga nasimulang programa at mas tutukan ang pangangailangan ng bawat komunidad, pamilya at kabataan," sabi ni Marcos sa Facebook page.
"Hindi ito dagdag na panahon sa puwesto. Dagdag itong panahon ng pananagutan sa taumbayan," dagdag pa niya.

Ipinasa ng Kongreso ang panukalang nagpapaliban sa nalalapit na BSKE at nagpapalawig sa termino ng mga opisyal sa limang taon. Ipinadala ang naturang batas sa Palasyo noong Huwebes para pirmahan ni Marcos upang ganap nang maging batas.
Kinumpirma rin ni Palace Press Officer Claire Castro ang paglagda sa panukala sa isang press briefing noong Biyernes.
“Pinirmahan na po ng Pangulo,” sabi ni Castro nang tanungin sa media briefing sa Ilocos Norte.
Sinabi ni Castro na kapuwa nakita ng Pangulo at mga mambabatas kung gaano kahalaga ang mga opisyal ng barangay, kabilang na sa paglaban sa kriminalidad at pagpapanatili ng kalinisan sa mga lansangan.

Ipinaliwanag din niya na nagbibigay-daan ang mas mahabang termino upang maisakatuparan ng mga opisyal ang mga pangmatagalang proyekto. Aniya, hindi ipinasa ang bagong batas para maging tamad ang mga opisyal.
“Ito ay para sila magtrabaho. Kaya para sa mga barangay officials, ang kailangan po namin ay trabaho mula sa inyo,” ani Castro.
Sa bagong batas, itinakda ang bagong petsa ng BSKE sa ikalawang linggo ng November 2028. Dapat sana itong gawin sa unang Lunes sa darating na Nobyembre.
Inaasahan naman na iaakyat ng mga kontra sa pagpapaliban ng naturang halalan ang usapin sa Korte Suprema. – FRJ GMA News

articles.title: Gilas Women fall short of Asian Games 3×3 gold vs hot-shooting Japan
articles.summary: Kacey dela Rosa puts Gilas Women on her back, but Japan proves too much to handle, pulling away for the convincing win behind its hot shooting to deal the Philippines its only loss in the Asian Games

blocks.text: SQUAD. Gilas Women in action in the women's 3x3 basketball competition in the 2026 Asian Games.
PSC-POC Media Pool
Kacey dela Rosa puts Gilas Women on her back, but Japan proves too much to handle, pulling away for the convincing win behind its hot shooting to deal the Philippines its only loss in the Asian Games

MANILA, Philippines – Gilas Women fell short of the Philippines’ third gold medal in the 2026 Asian Games after a stinging 21-11 loss to host Japan in the women’s 3×3 basketball final at the Kinjo Futo Station Square Venue in Nagoya on Friday, September 25.

Kacey dela Rosa put the the Filipinas on her back with 6 points, 3 rebounds, and 3 blocks, but the Japanese proved too much to handle, pulling away for the convincing win behind their hot shooting from beyond the arc.
Yuki Hirashita and Sakura Horiuchi fired 9 and 8 points, respectively, and each sank three two-pointers — the two taking turns in torching the Philippines.
Dela Rosa kept Gilas Women within striking distance with a bucket that cut their deficit to 8-12 before Japan closed out the win on a 9-3 run with 30 seconds to spare.
Hirashita scattered 5 points during that stretch, including the two-pointer that sealed the victory for Japan.
Amyah Espano put up 3 points and 3 rebounds in the silver finish, Kennan Ka added 2 points and 4 rebounds, while Maria Pasilang contributed 4 rebounds.
Despite the heartbreaking ending as they absorbed their only loss in the tournament, Gilas Women delivered the Philippines its first-ever 3×3 basketball medal in the Asian Games.
Meanwhile, Gilas Men missed out on the bronze after a 21-10 defeat to Iran.
Doy Dungo churned out 4 points, Luis Pablo tallied 3 points and 2 rebounds, Nic Cabañero had 2 points and 1 rebound, while Koji Buenaflor chimed in 1 point for the Philippines.
It was a disappointing result for Gilas Men after they won their first four games only to drop their last two matches, losing to South Korea in the semifinals and then to Iran. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Marcos suspends excise taxes on LPG, kerosene anew
articles.summary: The tax relief does not extend to gasoline and diesel, as Finance Secretary Frederick Go says this would 'not be progressive' because higher-income consumers who use more of the two fuels would…

blocks.text: A worker unloads tanks of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) at a store in Paco, Manila, on January 30, 2023.
Rappler

The tax relief does not extend to gasoline and diesel, as Finance Secretary Frederick Go says this would 'not be progressive' because higher-income consumers who use more of the two fuels would capture more of the benefit

items: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has suspended excise taxes on liquid petroleum gas (LPG) and kerosene due to high global oil prices, effective immediately upon publication.
The suspension lasts a maximum of three months and does not apply to gasoline or diesel, which have seen significant price increases.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has ordered the full suspension of excise taxes on liquid petroleum gas (LPG) and kerosene as high global oil prices continue to hit the wallets of Filipino consumers; the relief, however, does not extend to gasoline or diesel.

Marcos issued Executive Order No. 125 on Friday, September 25, following a recommendation from the Development Budget Coordination Committee (DBCC). The order will take effect immediately upon publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation.

The suspension covers LPG, except when used as a raw material for petrochemical production or for motive power, and kerosene, except when used as aviation fuel. Gasoline and diesel, which have seen successive sharp price increases in recent weeks, were not included in the tax break.

blocks.caption: Fuel prices rise again with big hike on September 22

blocks.text: The relief can last a maximum of three months, but may end earlier if the one-month average price of Dubai crude falls below the $80-per-barrel level.

The move came after the Department of Energy (DOE) certified that one-month average Dubai crude price had reached $99.41 per barrel, well above the $80-per-barrel threshold required for the government to suspend fuel excise taxes. The DBCC subsequently recommended full suspension.
The DBCC and DOE are also required to review the measure every month and may recommend whether the suspension should continue, be modified, or ended.

Finance Secretary Frederick Go earlier told senators that suspending excise taxes on gasoline and diesel would “not be progressive,” given that wealthier consumers use more of the two fuels and would capture a larger share of the benefit. The government could also lose about P12 billion in tax revenues each month if the break was extended to gasoline and diesel.

The government previously suspended excise taxes on LPG and kerosene for three months beginning in April after Dubai crude similarly breached the trigger threshold. Gasoline and diesel were also excluded from that earlier round.

The Department of Finance previously estimated that suspending excise taxes for LPG and kerosene for the maximum three-month period would cost the government around P4.1 billion in foregone revenues. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Jay-Z rape accuser says her allegation was false
articles.summary: A woman who accused Jay-Z of raping her when she was 13 now says she has never met the rap superstar.

blocks.text: A woman who accused Jay-Z of raping her when she was 13 has formally said her allegation was untrue.
The unnamed woman filed a lawsuit in 2024 claiming she had been drugged and raped by Jay-Z, real name Shawn Carter, and Sean "Diddy" Combs at a party after the MTV Video Music Awards in 2000.
The stars denied the allegation and she dropped the lawsuit last year. Carter then sued her and her lawyers.

In a statement filed in that case on Thursday, she wrote: "Shawn 'Jay-Z' Carter never raped me. I have never met or spoken to Mr. Carter. Mr. Carter never engaged in any inappropriate conduct toward me whatsoever."

The woman, known in court documents by the pseudonym Jane Doe, also said: "My claims that Mr Carter and Mr Combs raped me while a third celebrity, [name redacted] watched are false. There is no truth to any of my claims against Mr Carter.
"I understand my false accusations have caused Mr Carter immense pain, suffering, and damage that can never be fully undone."
Carter had vehemently denied the accusations, saying they were a "blackmail attempt" and describing them as "frivolous, fictitious and appalling allegations".
When the accuser dropped her case in February 2025, the rapper, who is married to singer Beyoncé, said: "The trauma that my wife, my children, loved ones and I have endured can never be dismissed."
The woman, from Alabama, has now been removed from Carter's lawsuit.
She said she had not received any money from the rap superstar or anyone acting on his behalf, and had not been paid to make her latest declaration.
The rapper is still suing the woman's former lawyers, led by Tony Buzbee.
In a statement to Rolling Stone, external, which first reported Jane Doe's new declaration, Buzbee said he had not seen it.

He said: "We have multiple lawyers (at least four) who dealt with Ms Doe long before she met me. She gave the exact same story to each. If for some reason now she is claiming she lied to us and the court, that's new information."

When Carter filed his lawsuit against the woman and her lawyers in February 2025, Buzbee claimed at the time that Carter's investigators had "repeatedly harassed, threatened and harangued this poor woman for weeks, trying to intimidate her and make her recant her story".
In her new declaration, the woman said: "I never received any threat from Mr Carter or anyone acting on his behalf."

Setting out the events that led to her allegation, the woman said she saw an advert on Facebook in September or October 2024 looking for people who might have sexual assault claims against Combs. "The ad triggered memories of being raped when I was 13 years old," she said.
She was contacted by a law firm but was not provided with a draft of the lawsuit containing her allegations and did not authorise it before it was filed in October 2024, she said.

She also said Buzbee and other lawyers acting on her behalf filed it "without conducting any independent investigation, background inquiry, or due diligence, and without obtaining any corroboration of the allegations".
She said: "The October Complaint alleges that Mr Carter and Mr Combs raped me when I was a minor while an unnamed celebrity watched. As discussed above, these allegations were false."
Buzbee also represents numerous other people who have made allegations against Combs.
Combs denied Jane Doe's claims, which his lawyer described at the time as one of a number of civil cases "pushed forward by an attorney more focused on media headlines than legal merit".
In July 2025, Combs was convicted by a criminal court on prostitution-related charges involving his two ex-girlfriends, and is currently serving a four-year prison sentence.
The BBC has contacted Buzbee for comment.

articles.title: Hurricane Polo barrels towards Baja California region of Mexico
articles.summary:
Area’s second-most intense hurricane on record being fuelled by exceptionally warm Pacific waters

Hurricane Polo is barreling towards the Baja California region of Mexico, the latest system…

blocks.text: Hurricane Polo is barreling towards the Baja California region of Mexico, the latest system in a Pacific hurricane season that has been notably active in recent months. On 22 September, a measurement of 892 millibars was registered for Hurricane Polo, making it the second-most intense hurricane on record in the east Pacific. It is fuelled by exceptionally warm waters across the Pacific Ocean, providing favourable conditions for the system to maintain its considerable strength.

Polo is expected to turn towards the west-north-west, before taking a more north-westerly trajectory on Saturday. It has maximum sustained winds of around 150mph, with even stronger gusts occurring within the most intense parts of the hurricane. Hurricane-force winds extend outward for approximately 40 miles from the centre, while tropical storm-force winds reach as far as 125 miles. These powerful winds, combined with torrential rainfall and dangerous seas, could have significant impacts. Although some fluctuations in intensity are possible over the coming days, Polo is expected to remain powerful as it tracks north-westwards.

In India, a deep 988-millibar low-pressure system – a tropical storm in this case – is centred along the east coast, bringing widespread and potentially disruptive weather conditions to Odisha and surrounding areas. The system is producing heavy rainfall across the region, with the latest forecast models suggesting totals could exceed 200mm in some locations over a 24-hour period. Rainfall rates are expected to be particularly intense at times, with hourly totals potentially exceeding 30mm in the heaviest downpours. Such intense rainfall could cause significant surface water and localised flooding, particularly in low-lying areas and places with poor drainage. Strong and gusty winds are also affecting coastal parts of Odisha. Winds are forecast to reach around 50-60mph, creating hazardous conditions in exposed areas and potentially causing disruption to travel, infrastructure and power supplies. Authorities have closed numerous schools across the affected districts for safety reasons.

Meanwhile, in Iberia, the relentless heat of summer is extending into meteorological autumn, with temperatures rising into the high 30s celsius on 23 September. Alvega, in Portugal, recorded a maximum temperature of 41.7C, smashing many July records from previous decades.

articles.title: Is Vince Dizon still in — or out — as DPWH chief?
articles.summary: 'Ovedue na po kayo ng ilang araw,' Senator Imee Marcos tells DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon

blocks.text: DPWH CHIEF. Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon leads the agency's flag-raising ceremony on October 20, 2025.
James Patrick Cruz/Rappler
'Ovedue na po kayo ng ilang araw,' Senator Imee Marcos tells DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon
It’s been more than a year since President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. tapped Vince Dizon to lead and clean up the corruption-tainted Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH).
But during the agency’s budget hearing at the Senate on Friday, September 25, Senator Imee Marcos raised a rather basic question: Is Dizon still legally in charge of DPWH?

Citing the Administrative Code of 1987, Marcos pointed out that a temporary designation in an acting capacity should not exceed one year. The safeguard is meant to prevent acting appointments from being used to circumvent the Commission on Appointments.
Dizon was appointed acting DPWH secretary on September 1, 2025, after his brief stint as transportation secretary.
On September 2, Marcos also sent a letter asking about the status of Dizon’s appointment. Dizon, apologetic, said he had yet to see the letter.
“Baka may appointment na kayo,” Marcos asked. (Maybe you already have an appointment.)
Dizon said his appointment as secretary continues until Congress adjourns and goes into recess. After that, he said, he would need to be reappointed.
Marcos, however, pointed back to the Administrative Code.
“Overdue na po kayo ng ilang araw,” (You’re already overdue for a few days) she told Dizon. “What’s the present status of your appointment?”
Dizon’s answer? He wasn’t exactly the person who could give it.
“Madam Senator, unfortunately, I’m not the appointing authority. I will confirm with the Office of the President and ask,” he said.
And who is the appointing authority? Marcos Jr., the senator’s estranged younger brother.
Senator Marcos then pressed Dizon on the legal basis for continuing to head the DPWH.
“If your appointment has lapsed, what’s the legal basis of appearing here?” she asked Dizon, whom she referred to as a friend.
Dizon’s explanation for why he was sitting there at the DPWH budget hearing?
“I’m here because I guess I’m not yet fired,” he said, while holding the back of his neck.
Marcos then asked if Dizon had been reappointed without anyone knowing. Marcos then cited information they had received that Dizon had been “appointed or reappointed” on July 27.
Dizon said he was not aware of any reappointment. According to his chief of staff, however, he could still perform his duties at the DPWH.
And despite the awkward questions over whether he still had the authority to lead the agency, Dizon appeared remarkably unfazed.
In fact, he seemed almost relieved by the possibility that his stint at the DPWH was over.

“Ma’am, this is music to my ears kasi medyo ayoko na rin pong nandito ako. Gusto ko pong wala na ako dito. Okay na po ito. Masaya pa po ako,” Dizon said. (Ma’am, this is music to my ears because, to be honest, I’m also getting tired of being here. I want to no longer be here. This is fine with me. I’d even be happy.)

“To be quite frank, it will be welcome kung totoo po ’yung sinasabi ninyo na hindi na ako secretary ng DPWH. I’ll be more than happy to accept that kasi napakahirap po ng trabahong ito,” he said. (To be quite frank, it would be welcome if what you’re saying is true that I’m no longer the DPWH secretary. I’d be more than happy to accept that because this job is extremely difficult.)
So is he in or out? – Rappler.com

articles.title: Villanueva wants firing squad for guilty in flood control scheme
articles.summary: Senator Joel Villanueva on Friday called for those proven guilty in the alleged flood control scam to face the firing squad. “I am always for justice. Until now, gusto ko ngang i-firing squad yung…

blocks.text: Published September 25, 2026 6:10pm
Senator Joel Villanueva on Friday called for those proven guilty in the alleged flood control scam to face the firing squad.

During the Senate budget hearing for the Commission on Higher Education and state universities and colleges, Villanueva asked University of the Philippines Resilience Institute executive director Mahar Lagmay whether there were better ways to forecast extreme weather events.
Villanueva then expressed frustration over recurring flooding in his home province of Bulacan before turning to the alleged flood control scam, in which he had previously been linked.

“God knows, and until now, some people thought that I have a case on this. Until now wala ‘ho akong case. May complaints, etc. tinuturo na kasama ako ngayon… and I’m not scared to talk about this,” Villanueva said.
(God knows, and until now, some people thought that I have a case on this. Until now, I do not have a case. There are complaints, etc. and I am being implicated… I am not afraid to talk about this.)

“I am always for justice. Until now, gusto ko ngang i-firing squad iyong lahat ng may kaso dito na talagang mapapatunayan na parte nitong scheme na ito, itong kalokohan na ito, itong kabulastugan na nangyari dahil number one na naapektuhan yung probinsya namin sa Bulacan,” Villanueva said.

(I am always for justice, I want a firing squad for all those who have a case in this and will be proven guilty that they have a part in this scheme, this bluff because number one affected is our province of Bulacan.)
Villanueva said that the records would show that he spent years asking the Department of Public Works and Highways for an integrated flood control program.

During the height of the flood control issue in 2025, dismissed Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) district engineer Henry Alcantara tagged several lawmakers in the multi-billion corruption scheme. — including Villanueva.
Alcantara claimed that he brought P150 million to a rest house in Bulacan, which was allegedly received by one of Villanueva’s staff.
No formal charges have been lodged against the Bulacan senator.

Accused alongside him were Sen. Jinggoy Estrada and former senator Bong Revilla. Both of whom were indicted for charges in relation to the flood control scam. While Revilla was able to post bail, Estrada remains incarcerated at the Quezon City Jail.
The Philippines abolished the death penalty in 2006 under Republic Act No. 9346, replacing capital punishment with life imprisonment and reclusion perpetua.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Sandiganbayan orders Romualdez to show up on October 12 bail hearing
articles.summary: The Sandiganbayan has ordered former Speaker and Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez to appear before the anti-graft court on October 12 for the first day of his bail hearing.

blocks.text: Published September 25, 2026 5:51pm
The Sandiganbayan has ordered former Speaker and Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez to appear before the anti-graft court on October 12 for the first day of his bail hearing.

This was contained in the Sandiganbayan Third Division’s order issued Friday, September 25, in connection with the P7.4-billion plunder charge filed against Romualdez and three others over their alleged links to the flood control controversy.

“Accused Romualdez is required to be present and sign the pre-trial order during the initial bail hearing on October 12, 2026, at 8:30 in the morning,” read the court order, which was issued after the termination of the pre-trial conference or the court process where the evidence for both parties are marked, read.

The anti-graft court also said in the same order that Romualdez is expected to file his petition for bail on Monday, September 28, an information that was also told to reporters by Romualdez’s counsel, Ade Fajardo.
Romualdez attended the pre-trial conference virtually from his cell in New Quezon City Jail on Friday since he is still being treated for his brain and heart-related ailments.

Accordingly, the Sandiganbayan set the bail hearings on the Romualdez case on October 12, 2026, and every Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday thereafter, except on legal holidays and on the day the court has an official activity, all at 8:30 in the morning and 1:30 in the afternoon.
The prosecution, for its part, is expected to present 23 witnesses during the bail hearings.
The anti-graft court ordered the prosecution to submit its list of by Friday, October 2, 2026, alongside the schedule indicating which witnesses will be presented on each hearing date.
The presentation of evidence for the P7.4 billion case, on the other hand, is set on November 23, 2026, and every Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday thereafter. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: US backs Elon Musk's bid to overturn €120m EU fine against X
articles.summary: The EU had said X "deceives users" by selling blue ticks without "meaningfully verifying" accounts.

blocks.text: The US government is seeking to join Elon Musk's legal challenge to overturn a €120m (£105m) EU fine against X over its blue tick badges.

In December 2025, the European Commission said the platform "deceives users" by allowing people to pay for a blue verified check mark, because it is not "meaningfully verifying" who is behind the account.
But US Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate said on Thursday that the commission had "inappropriately attempted" to expand its reach to American companies outside its control.
Musk, who spent millions helping elect Donald Trump and other Republicans, has previously claimed EU tech regulation "inhibits progress" for companies.
The US Department of Justice (DOJ) has filed an application, external with the EU's General Court in support of Musk's and X's attempts to dismiss ​the case.

It claims that under a section of law in the Statute of the Court of Justice of the EU, a state may intervene in disputes before the court if it "can establish an interest in the result of the case to the court".
The DOJ said the US "has a clear interest" in ensuring any decision by the commission was applied consistently with "how territorial jurisdiction is generally understood in international law".
It also wants to make sure it would not "otherwise prejudice" US-headquartered digital services that "contribute significantly" to its economy.
In a press briefing on Friday, external, European Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier said it was "ready to defend" its position in court.
He added that the commission had an "solid case" at its disposal, due to the alleged breach of its Digital Services Act.
In addition to its use of blue ticks, EU regulators had accused X of failing to provide transparency around its adverts and denying researchers access to public data.

Henna Virkkunen, the regulator's executive vice-president for tech sovereignty, said at the time of the fine's issue it was "holding X responsible for undermining users' rights and evading accountability".
"Deceiving users with blue checkmarks, obscuring information on ads and shutting out researchers have no place online in the EU," she said.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) had criticised the EU regulator, accusing it of attacking and censoring US firms.
"The European Commission's fine isn't just an attack on X, it's an attack on all American tech platforms and the American people by foreign governments," Rubio wrote in a post on X.
"The days of censoring Americans online are over."
His remarks were reposted by Musk, who added "absolutely".
The European Commission denied targeting any specific nationality, stating it is simply protecting its digital and democratic standards to maintain its role as a global benchmark.
The action marked the Commission's first official non-compliance decision under the Digital Services Act (DSA), one of two mandatory rulebooks governing online platforms in the EU.

However, the EU is also conducting several other investigations into the platform, including one into its integrated AI assistant Grok over concerns it was used to create sexualised images of real people.

articles.title: Carlos Yulo falls short of parallel bars medal, concludes stellar Asian Games
articles.summary: Carlos Yulo narrowly misses out on a parallel bars bronze that would have been the cherry on top of his superb Asian Games run that saw him win back-to-back gold medals in floor exercise and vault

blocks.text: FOCUSED. The Philippines' Carlos Edriel Yulo in action during the men's parallel bars final of the Asian Games.
Edgar Su/REUTERS
Carlos Yulo narrowly misses out on a parallel bars bronze that would have been the cherry on top of his superb Asian Games run that saw him win back-to-back gold medals in floor exercise and vault
MANILA, Philippines – It may not have been the perfect ending, but Carlos Yulo has already given the country plenty of reasons to celebrate.

Yulo fell short of a third artistic gymnastics medal as he wrapped up his campaign in the 2026 Asian Games with a fourth-place finish in the men’s parallel bars at the Nagoya General Gymnasium on Friday, September 25.

The double Olympic gold medalist registered 14.3 points, just barely missing out on a bronze that would have been the cherry on top of a superb Asian Games run that saw him win back-to-back gold medals in floor exercise and vault.

With hardly any surprise, reigning two-time Olympic champion Zou Jingyuan struck gold with an unrivaled 15.5 points — a full point ahead of Japan’s Shinnosuke, who settled for silver with 14.5 points.
Zou completed an Asian Games three-peat in the apparatus after also reigning in 2018 in Indonesia and in 2023 in China.
Uzbekistan’s Rasuljon Abdurakhimov edged Yulo for the bronze with 14.433 points.
Despite coming up short, Yulo has done his part, breaking the Philippines’ golden ice in this Asian Games with not just one, but two titles in his pet events.

In fact, Yulo is the only athlete in men’s artistic gymnastics to win gold medals in multiple apparatuses in this edition. Zou and Chinese teammates Zhang Boheng and Lan Xingyu also own two golds, although the other came in the team event.

With his latest triumphs, Yulo has completed his collection, adding a pair of Asian Games golds to a trophy case already filled with titles from the Olympics, World Championships, Asian Championships, World Cup, and Southeast Asian Games. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Volkswagen, Audi to recall almost 1 million cars in Germany
articles.summary: Volkswagen and its subsidiary Audi are to recall nearly a million vehicles in Germany due to a potential steering fault.

image.caption: Volkswagen is to recall nearly a million vehicles in Germany due to a potential steering faultImage: Moritz Frankenberg/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Germany auto firm Volkswagen (VW) and its daughter company Audi are to recall nearly a million vehicles in Germany due to steering problems, according to German media reports.

The KBA road traffic authority was cited by the t-online news portal as saying that the recall was required due to potential bolt failures that could damage the steering gearbox or, in some cases, cause a complete loss of steering.
The bolts are to be replaced with ones resistant to corrosion caused by humidity.
Autor Motor Sport magazine reported that VW believed the steering issue would impact only a smaller proportion of the recalled vehicles.
The company said there were no known cases of accidents or injuries caused by the possible bolt failure.
According to KBA, the VW models Tiguan, Touran, Golf Variant, Caddy und Golf produced between September 24, 2013, and July 1, 2024, are impacted by the recall.
This is equivalent to around 900,000 vehicles in Germany and 2.16 million around the world.
For Audi, 700,000 vehicles around the world are impacted by the problem, including 58,555 in Germany.
The recall comes as VW grapples with dwindling sales in recent years, with the firm laying off tens of thousands of staff and shrinking plants in order to cut costs.

articles.title: Why farmers are pairing crops with solar panels
articles.summary: From cooler soil to paid grazing land, farmers are finding solar panels can do more than generate power.

image.caption: An agrivoltaic pilot project shades a pear orchard in Llupia, France, part of a push to protect crops from droughts, frost and other extreme weatherImage: Michel Clementz/MAXPPP/picture alliance

blocks.text: Traditionally, solar panel farms are quiet — save for the faint hum of the inverter. But on about one in ten of American solar farms, there's a new sound reverberating through fields: baaaa.
Letting sheep roam under solar panels is just one of many forms of a burgeoning strategy called agrivoltaics, where crops grow or livestock graze in tandem with renewable energy infrastructure.

It's not only of potential benefit for the animals, which get additional shade. The panels can also protect crops from the elements as well as divert water to them, creating cooler, damper conditions that even boost yields.
And even the solar panels themselves tend to respond well to this co-existence — as the cooler they are, the more electricity they produce per watt of sunlight.

"Having concrete or something underneath the solar panels — you're going to have lower efficiency than having something like plants that are transpiring and cooling off on the land surface," Carl Bernacchi, professor of plant biology and crop sciences at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, told DW.

While the potential is enormous, especially as climate change puts more and more heat stress on agriculture, the practice is still in its infancy. In Europe, if agrivoltaics were implemented on just 1% of available agricultural land, the continent could exceed its solar energy targets for 2030.
But uptake has been slow: agrivoltaics represents just 18.4 gigawatts of energy worldwide as of mid-2025, less than 1% of the world's solar capacity.

blocks.caption: Sheep graze under solar panels in Guizhou province, southwest China, part of a growing practice of pairing livestock with solar energy productionImage: Tao Liang/Xinhua/picture alliance

blocks.text: What thrives under the panels

The idea for agrivoltaics dates back to 1981, when two German scientists published an article titled "Kartoffeln unter dem Kollektor" (or "Potatoes beneath the collector"). But the first pilot project didn't begin until 2004 in Japan, a land-constrained country, where there's particular concern over balancing solar deployment with the protection of farmland.

There are three main types of agrivoltaics: horizontal, where panels look directly up at the sky, vertical, where they're placed in large rows, perpendicular to the ground, and integrated, often installed atop greenhouses.
Research suggests shade-tolerant crops stand to benefit. That includes berries, grapes and tomatoes — where the panels' steel framing often doubles as trellises — as well as peaches and peppers.
The panels can also prevent water from fully evaporating, creating a more humid microclimate that benefits the soil — though humidity is a double-edged sword, sometimes introducing plant disease.

Sheep have also proven to be a particularly good match. Compared to cattle or goats, they're generally easier to manage around solar infrastructure, less likely to damage equipment, and small enough to fit comfortably beneath panels. The practice has other sustainability upsides too: sheep manure fertilizes the soil, and sites require less herbicide.

"If we look at the sheep industry, this has been a real paradigm shift for them, where instead of having to pay to lease land to graze their animals — now they're actually getting paid to graze," Kinzer said. "So it completely puts the economics on its head and is a huge opportunity for the sheep industry, which is really struggling in the US pretty much since World War II."

blocks.caption: Solar panels raised on steel supports shade a French orchard, one of several agrivoltaic setups now in use across EuropeImage: Michel Clementz/MAXPPP/picture alliance

blocks.text: A double climate win
Agrivoltaics sit at a rare intersection of climate mitigation (cutting emissions) and adaptation (adjusting to a warming planet).
"It is both, which is pretty unique as far as climate solutions go," Kinzer said.

The practice offers one answer to where solar panels could go, helping to produce cheaper and more efficient energy, while also benefiting crops that might struggle due to rising temperatures or volatile weather.

And research suggests that climate change will only make regions grow drier, "broadening areas where agrivoltaics can mitigate crop yield penalties (even boosting yield) and improve overall profitability," writeresearchers in a journal article for Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS).
A dual-income stream can also offer farmers some insurance should temperature or weather knock out a season's plantings.
"Being able to have that alternate form of income, it's massive for folks who are depending on weather to make their living that is becoming increasingly more extreme and varied," Kinzer said.
Tamil Nadu farmers learn to thrive despite water scarcity
Not every farm benefits
So why has adoption been so slow?
"In theory, it's a win-win scenario," Bernacchi said. "But of course, with any technologies, there are always caveats and issues."

One reason is that agrivoltaics don't work everywhere. In America's arid West, where heat stress and less available water can threaten crops, yields stayed the same or even rose under panels. In the humid Midwest, on the other hand, panel shading limited photosynthesis and led to reduced yields in maize and soybeans.
For cash crops, where there's a very small margin for profit, even a minor reduction in yield is a no-go for many farmers.

Then there's the expense. For solar producers, every added inch to mount panels higher means more labor and steel costs. And farmers might need to find new equipment or change methods to adapt to a new system.

"Farmers want to learn from other farmers," said Kinzer, who works with farmers across the US to see how agrivoltaics are being adopted. "They want to hear from folks who are doing it. And so there's a little bit of a chicken-and-the-egg problem for farmers: In most cases, they can't just go across the street or into the next county over and see a project like this and talk to the farmers doing it."
Bridging the divide between farmers and solar

Solar power's land footprint has made it controversial in certain communities — some farming associations have protested converting farmland into acres of solar panels, arguing their members cease to be farmers and become energy producers instead.
It's a tension agrivoltaics helps to address.

One surveyfound that more than 80% of Americans would be more likely to support solar development in their community, if it allowed for the co-production of energy and agriculture — about 10% more than those that support solar development in general.

"There's this cultural conflict between the farmers who want to farm and the solar companies that want to produce electricity," Bernacchi said. "And agrivoltaics really does bill itself as sort of a middle ground. You can still farm and still get the electricity from the same land."
Agrivoltaic combines solar power and agriculture

articles.title: P.E.I. woman who lost nearly $10K in bitcoin scam wants bank to reimburse her money
articles.summary: Binh Tran has spent the last six months trying to get her money back after falling victim to a scam call.

image.caption: A statement from TD Bank says it understands that it can be 'distressing to be impacted by a scam.' (Ken Linton/CBC)

blocks.text: PEI
Binh Tran has spent the last six months trying to get her money back after falling victim to a scam call.
Binh Tran searched caller's number and found it was the same as on the bank's website
Woman who lost almost $10K in bitcoin scam says banks 'don't care about the customer'
One morning in March, she answered a call from someone claiming to be from TD Bank's fraud prevention department who told her she was needed for an investigation.
"He told me that I … need to withdraw my money for safety," she said.
She was told to stay on the phone while she entered the bank. She withdrew money through a teller and later deposited it into a bitcoin machine for verification.
She felt something was wrong, but she searched online and found the number the scammer used was the same as what was listed on the bank's website, leading her to believe the call was real.
In total, she lost $9,800. Earlier this month, she was informed by TD Bank that she would not be reimbursed.
"I think that the TD Bank, they didn't do anything for investigation," she said.
"They don't care about a customer. They don't care about a customer loss."

items: P.E.I. couple says their kids' RESP is in limbo because the bank altered their last name
Policy requiring P.E.I. seniors to produce bank statements will be changed, minister says

blocks.text: In a statement, TD Bank declined to comment on details of specific cases and said it understands it can be "distressing" to fall victim to a scam. The bank said it takes reports of fraud "very seriously."
"I can confirm TD thoroughly reviewed this matter, shared our findings with Binh, and explained to her the rationale behind our decision," a spokesperson wrote in the statement.
"Helping protect our clients remains a top priority. We have multiple layers of security, monitoring and customer education in place."

TD offered tips to protect against fraud, including not trusting unsolicited calls and not assuming a phone number is legitimate. It also noted that TD "will never ask" a customer for assistance with an investigation or request passwords or one-time security codes sent to mobile devices or email.
The issue for Tran lies with a form she signed when withdrawing the money with the teller, which takes responsibility off of TD Bank to reimburse her money.

It reads that the bank "has warned me that fraudsters may ask their victims to purchase gift cards or bitcoin," and that the customer confirmed that the withdrawal was made of their "own free will, without any coercion or pressure from a third party."
Tran also got police involved, speaking with an officer and filing a report. However, she is not sure how the investigation is progressing.

She said she doesn't agree with TD and plans to appeal the bank's decision to the federal banking ombudsman, noting she took the care to check that the bank's phone number was correct and that she had no reason not to trust it.
"I just work at a Superstore at [a] part-time job, so this is a huge amount. This is my retirement nest, so I cannot lose that amount," she said.
"I just want my money back to my account. It's not easy."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Lucas McInnis is a journalist at CBC Prince Edward Island. He can be reached at lucas.mcinnis@cbc.ca.

Germany's Heidenau bans new Stolpersteine dedicated to victims of Holocaust

The town of Heidenau, near Dresden, has banned new Stolpersteine (stumbling stones) on the public streets, with the center-right CDU and the far-right AfD voting together to curb the installation of new memorial plaques bearing the names of Holocaust victims.

The city's administration urged against the motion. The initiators, however, argued that placing the plaques in the street leads to "passersby walking over or even stepping onto the names of the victims." They suggested honoring Holocaust victims at one of the city's cemeteries instead.
Stumbling stones — against forgetting

With the local branch of Friedrich Merz's CDU joining forces with the AfD to pass the motion, it has also raised questions about the political "firewall" against the far right pledged by mainstream German parties.
The International Auschwitz Committee described the CDU support as scandalous.

"This is a transparent and despicable attempt to drive Nazi victims in Heidenau out of the city once again and dispose of them where, according to the AfD, their memory has belonged a long time ago — at the cemetery," said the organization's Executive Vice President Christoph Heubner.

articles.title: Italy to ban burqa in schools, limit foreign pupils
articles.summary: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s government has passed new school rules capping the number of students who don't speak fluent Italian and banning face coverings.

image.caption: Meloni said the burqa ban was 'a matter of security' Image: Alessandra Tarantino/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Italy's conservative government on Thursday approved a new decree banning face-covering Islamic veils — including burqas and niqabs — in schools and putting a limit on the number of students with a poor command of the Italian language in each classroom.

Italian Prime Minister, Giorgia Meloni, called her Cabinet's measures "tools of common sense that do not divide," adding that they will help integration by avoiding what the right-wing leader called "ghetto classes."
She went on to say the rules would lead to all students receiving the "same opportunities."

Opposition parties and other critics have denounced the move by Meloni's government, with some calling it a "witch hunt” and others accusing the government of turning immigration into more of a political issue ahead of next year's general election.
What do Italy's new school rules entail?
The measures take effect right away but still require parliamentary approval within 60 days. Meloni's coalition currently holds a majority in the country's legislature.
Here is what the decree includes:

items: A per-classroom cap of 30% for foreign students who lack sufficient proficiency in Italian
In primary schools, the limit applies to pupils without Italian citizenship who were not born in Italy or did not attend at least two years of preschool
In lower and upper secondary schools, the same limit applies to students without Italian citizenship who have not attended the country's school system for at least three years
Failure to comply with the decree is punishable by a fine of up to €1,000 euros ($1,140)

blocks.text: Face-coverings banned in schools
The decree bans burqas and niqabs in schools but will continue to allow hijabs.
Meloni said the burqa ban was "a matter of security."

"When a woman — or worse, a young girl — is forced to cover her face, she is being denied fundamental rights and the very integration that is so often loudly championed," Meloni was quoted as saying in a television interview.
Italian Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara said the decree would affect about 1,000 classrooms, which come up to 0.3% of the nationwide tally.
According to official data, pupils without Italian citizenship comprised 11.2% of Italy's school population from 2022 to 2023, while classes with over 30% foreign students stood at 7.6% of the total.
What do critics say?
Opponents of the decree are worried that the new measure could force students to attend schools far from the neighborhoods where they live.
Reports have also highlighted concerns among school authorities regarding how the rules would work in areas with large migrant populations.

Independent child rights organization Save the Children had on Wednesday called on the Italian government to weigh the measure "with the utmost political responsibility,” adding that it risked creating discriminatory effects.
"Such a criterion would create ‘first-class' and 'second-class' students," the organization said in its statement.
Meanwhile, opposition leader Elly Schlein railed against the decree, accusing Meloni's government of "a new witch hunt at the expense of children."

articles.title: AI 'slop' is dominating menus, as some restaurant owners turn to it to save time and money
articles.summary: Diners have taken to social media to share photos of overly-shiny sandwiches and circular shrimp, lamenting the suspected use of AI. But some in the restaurant business say it's helped them reduce…

image.caption: A burger ordered from The Fancy Induced Burger pictured beside an AI-enhanced image of the product, taken at the chain's Waterloo location on Thursday. (James Dunne/CBC)

blocks.text: Business·New

Diners have taken to social media to share photos of overly-shiny sandwiches and circular shrimp, lamenting the suspected use of AI. But some in the restaurant business say it's helped them reduce costs and save time in a notoriously difficult industry.
AI use could be problem if it misrepresents the product, but false advertising not a big concern, experts say
From cartoonish-looking sandwiches to doughnut-shaped shrimp, AI might be on the menu at your local fast-food restaurant.

Diners have taken to the internet to share photos of sandwich boards and window displays bearing food they say looks rubbery, surreal and seems to be created with artificial intelligence tools — which have made it increasingly easy to generate visuals on the cheap.

"This looks like what aliens would put in a presentation about what Earth food is," a Reddit user captioned in a post accompanied by a picture of a sandwich board with breaded shrimp and gyros with suspiciously geometric textures.
Others described a CNE sandwich they assumed to be AI-generated as "uncanny and nauseating" and "slop."
And for some Toronto customers, these kinds of images aren't just stomach-turning — they take them as a signal of the restaurant's values.
"I feel like it's really inauthentic and it doesn't make me wanna go eat at your restaurant," said Cynthia Lem.
For her, AI-generated imagery raises questions about what the actual food would look like once it arrives, making her wary of any establishments using the technology.
The death of folk graphic design in favor of AI slop across our country's delis is leading to some incredibly Lovecraftian food horrors pic.twitter.com/snDyC675Ei—samfbiddle

While some consumers say these images are ruining their appetites and raising worries about possible misrepresentations of menu items, those in the restaurant business say it's helped them reduce costs in a notoriously difficult industry. And marketing experts say use of the tech isn't necessarily bad if it's done thoughtfully.
Not all AI use created equally

Before taking a single bite, restaurant-goers rely heavily on imagery to dictate what they order, according to business consultant and Schulich School of Business marketing professor David Pullara. And that means businesses relying on heavy-handed AI imagery are taking a big risk.
"Great food photography sells," said Pullara. "So if you're using AI to generate an image that's terrible, it's going to hurt your sales, it's going to hurt your brand."

But while some consumers might object to the use of AI on principle, he thinks the risk of using it to enhance food photography is low if done well — especially if it can help small- and medium-sized businesses manage their costs.

Restaurant businesses face thin margins, often making it difficult to turn a profit. According to Restaurants Canada's most recent survey of some of its members, 41 per cent said they were operating at a loss or just breaking even, with rising fuel costs only exacerbating issues.

items: Canadian restaurants struggling to turn a profit, new report says

blocks.text: Pullara says hiring a professional photographer is expensive, and might be out of budget for a small restaurant business. For that reason, taking a high-resolution photo of food and using an AI application to make small tweaks could create an image worthy of putting on a menu, Pullara says.

"I don't think it's the AI that makes the image unappealing. I think the problem is asking AI for a photo and just not using a common-sense filter about [whether] this actually looks good," Pullara said.
That tweaking of real photos is how the marketing team at The Fancy Induced Burger uses AI.

A marketing manager for the Canadian franchise, Fez Mian, says he'll snap a picture of a burger as it comes out of the kitchen and run it through an AI application like ChatGPT, prompting it to enhance the texture and freshness of menu items. Those images are used across the business — on menus, in-store posters and online.

The company doesn't rely on professional photographers or graphic designers as much these days as a result. That's saved them money and time, as Mian no longer needs to book a photographer, wait for the shoot date and then wait to receive the images before using them in marketing.
"We're not, like, spending endless time planning and scheduling and whatnot," Mian said. "Within … five minutes, 10 minutes it's out the door."
That speed is especially important on social media, Mian says, enabling them to create and post new content more frequently.
Does AI cross the line into false advertising?
For some consumers, the worry is about how the food item that shows up on their plate will compare to the enhanced image on the menu.
AI food pics on restaurant menus are killing customers' appetites
If AI imagery is vastly different from the actual product, Rotman School of Management marketing professor David Soberman says that could be a problem.

"You wanna make your products look good, but you don't want your products to be misleading," Soberman said. If an AI-enhancement makes a steak look like it's an inch thick but the actual product is half the size, for example, that would be a problem.

But the same is true for food imagery enhanced using run-of-the-mill staging and image editing, Soberman says. Both Soberman and Pullara say they don't think AI imagery generally raises the likelihood of misleading consumers, especially since most have come to accept that images on menu boards will look better than the real deal.

"I think people just kind of know that there's going to be some variance between what you're seeing on these professionally shot, produced photos and what you actually can have prepared in the back of the kitchen in two minutes," Pullara said.

At The Fancy Induced Burger, Mian says there's always a human involved in checking the company's AI-enhanced images to make sure no extra ingredients were added in the process that might mislead customers.
Still, Toronto-based food stylist Zoe Rousseau says they think the work they do is more authentic than AI-generated food imagery.

Despite some common misconceptions based on industry standards from decades ago, Rousseau says food staging doesn't involve fake food most of the time. Instead, they take their time to pick the best-looking ingredients, make sure they're perfectly placed, and work with a team of photographers and prop stylists who help achieve a beautiful end product.
Rousseau says they understand why small businesses trying to cut down costs would try AI, but if the generated imagery simply "doesn't look like the food," it won't work to pull customers in.
"I think that restaurateurs are better off taking pictures with their iPhone," Rousseau said.

For that reason, they're not too worried about AI coming for their job. They hope that the backlash to AI menu items might even compel more businesses to invest in stylists and photographers, boosting their industry.
"I can play with texture and I can play with angles," Rousseau said. "Just the freshness of it … the AI can't do that."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Abby Hughes is a writer with CBC News based in Toronto. Originally from Orillia, Ont., she studied journalism at Toronto Metropolitan University. She covers news from the worlds of business, entertainment, health, science and education, and her favourite stories focus on the real people in those areas — the customers, fans, patients, citizens and students. You can reach her with story ideas at abby.hughes@cbc.ca.
With files from Lauren Battagello, James Dunne and Nisha Patel

Pope Leo will visit France this weekend, the first papal state visit to the country in 18 years, beginning with Paris today.

During the visit, Leo is expected to seek to repair the Catholic Church’s standing after abuse scandals in the country, as well as deliver a landmark speech on AI development at Unesco and talk about Europe’s future in Metz, with some other European leaders expected to attend.
He will visit the restored Notre Dame Cathedral in Paris, as well as the famed Catholic shrine in Lourdes, among other places.

blocks.text: Pope Leo lands in Paris
As I was chatting about politics, Pope Leo’s plane has just landed in Paris.
We should see him shortly.

blocks.caption: President Emmanuel Macron speaks during an interview with France 2 and TF1 at the Elysee Presidential Palace, in Paris. Photograph: Ludovic Marin/AFP/Getty Images

Former president Nicolas Sarkozy said the decision was Macron’s personal choice, adding that he would have attended if he were still in office.

articles.title: Ethiopia: Internet disrupted in Tigray amid conflict escalation
articles.summary: A web monitor reported an internet disruption in northern Ethiopia amid renewed fighting between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and the federal government.

image.caption: Tigrayans rushed to buy supplies after renewed fighting between the TPLF militia and the Ethiopian stateImage: AFP

blocks.text: Access to the internet has been disrupted in northern Ethiopia's Tigray region, the web monitor NetBlocks reported on Friday.
The region has been the site of renewed hostilities this week that shattered a 2022 peace deal between Ethiopia and the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) militia.
During the 2020-2022 Tigray war, the region was largely cut off from the outside world and hundreds of thousands of people were left in famine-like conditions.
"Confirmed: Network data indicate a subnational disruption in ⁠northern ⁠Ethiopia corresponding to reports of a telecoms blackout in Tigray," NetBlocks said.
The cause of the disruption was not immediately clear.
The Reuters news agency cited Tigray residents saying panic buying left shop shelves empty.
"There is deep fear that banks, telecom networks, electricity and basic goods could be cut off again," a local resident told the AFP news agency, adding that there was "panic in the community."
The new rebel alliance transforming the Tigray conflict
TPLF offensive sparks fear of return to war

The TPLF took control of regional airports in Tigray earlier this week and also clashed with government forces in the neighboring Afar and Amhara regions. The militia said it was now in "full-blown war" with Addis Ababa.
The group also formed an anti-government alliance with the Fano militia in Amhara and five other armed groups.
In the 2022-2023 war, Fano fought alongside the federal government against the Tigrayan rebels.
The TPLF ruled Ethiopia from 1991 to 2018 and was later sidelined alongside the rise of Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.

articles.title: Africa's richest man helps fund $660m fuel pipeline between Ethiopia and Djibouti
articles.summary: The pipeline would strengthen energy security in landlocked Ethiopia, while creating jobs at Djibouti's port.

blocks.text: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote, Ethiopia and Djibouti have agreed to develop a $660m (£500m) petroleum pipeline and storage project linking the two countries.
The project will include a 120km- (75 mile-) pipeline connecting Djibouti's Damerjog port to a distribution facility in Dewele, Ethiopia, as well as storage capacity of about 400 million litres.
It is expected to begin operations within 18 months.
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed said the pipeline would reduce the time needed to transport fuel from Djibouti's port to the Ethiopian capital, Addis Ababa, from five days to one.
The first phase will transport key petroleum products, including jet fuel, diesel and petrol.
Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony, Dangote said the project would strengthen Ethiopia's energy security and make its fuel supply chain more resilient.

Landlocked Ethiopia relies heavily on Djibouti's port for imports, including petroleum products. The new infrastructure is expected to reduce pressure on existing transport systems supporting industries, including transport, aviation, agriculture and construction.
Djibouti is also expected to benefit from increased port activity, job creation and higher government revenues.
The project is part of Dangote's wider expansion of infrastructure and manufacturing businesses across Africa.

Dangote Cement has production capacity of about 55 million tonnes a year, while his oil refinery in Nigeria currently has capacity to process 700,000 barrels of crude a day and is seeking to double that to 1.4 million barrels a day.
The refinery recently listed 4.1 billion ordinary shares on the Nigerian stock exchange, aiming to raise about $1.63bn (£1.2bn).
In Kenya, the company is due to break ground next week on a proposed 700,000-barrel-a-day crude oil refinery in Lamu.

articles.title: ‘Wake-up call’: Labor considers changing Australian laws after OpenAI Medicare hack
articles.summary:
Expert says Australia’s criminal laws should be clarified to determine how fault is applied to a corporation when its AI agent commits a crime

The federal government could change Australian…

blocks.text: The federal government could change Australian laws if the current legal framework could not respond to the unprecedented OpenAI hack of Medicare, ministers have confirmed.

On Friday, the government said the review by spy agency, the Australian signals directorate, would consider whether legislative change was needed after the prime minister revealed an artificial intelligence agent developed by OpenAI hacked Medicare’s statistics website and three other systems in June.
If current laws could not touch the tech giant, they would need updating, environment minister Murray Watt said on Friday.

“There’s now a review of this underway through that task force that we’ve appointed, and one of the things that they’ll be looking at is whether these matters can be referred to the Australian federal police under current Australian law,” he told Channel Seven’s Sunrise program.
“If that is possible to happen, then that will happen. If it’s not possible, then clearly that indicates that we need to change Australian laws, and that’s what we’ll be doing.”

The assistant minister for technology and the digital economy, Andrew Charlton, acknowledged similar incidents would become “more and more prevalent into the future” and the government would need to be prepared.

“That’s why we’re conducting a review of the incident as well as a review of the laws to determine exactly … whether there needs to be legislative change to recognise this type of incident conducted by an AI agent rather than directly by a person or a company,” Charlton told ABC radio.
Labor has announced it would legislate an AI standard, which Charlton said would be informed by the rapid review. The government has said it wants the bill to be introduced by the end of the year.

UNSW professor Lyria Bennett Moses, an academic expert in technology and law, said Australia’s criminal laws should be clarified to determine how fault, such as intention or knowledge, is applied to a corporation when its AI agent commits a crime.
She said existing laws are clear if a human or corporation gains unauthorised access to restricted data, but it’s more complicated when an AI agent commits the physical element of the offence.
“The person is not the AI agent, so it’s not about what the AI agent intended. It’s about how you attribute that intention and that knowledge back to a corporation,” Bennett Moses said.

Bennett Moses said existing civil laws are more likely to deal with these sorts of incidents, that would allow a government or individual to seek compensation an AI company for harm “negligently caused by that corporation”.

“If their systems have suffered harm and there is financial loss, and that harm was caused by the negligence of a corporation, you’ve got a potential for litigation to get compensation for that harm,” she said.
“Here it seems to me much easier to hold a company liable, because if a company caused the harm, it’s not a defence to say that my bot did it.”
Anthony Albanese told the Asia Society on Thursday that the incident was a “wake-up call” about the risks of AI, and whether humans would remain in charge of the technology.
“This technology is moving very, very fast, and we need to make sure that we have a responsibility to keep on top of it,” Albanese said.
On Friday, the prime minister addressed the United Nations and called on other countries to act to “shape artificial intelligence development, rather than be passively shaped by it”.
The opposition leader, Angus Taylor, told reporters the opposition would be open to working with the government to hold companies accountable.

“I’ve long believed that data breaches need to be dealt with in an appropriate way and those responsible for the data breaches need to be accountable for it … But we’ll wait and see what the government has in mind.”

OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said on Thursday the company was conducting an extensive review of “misaligned model activity during training and evaluation” and was “notifying third parties when our review identifies potential impacts to their systems”.

“During this review, we identified activity involving several Australian government websites and services as our models attempted to look up answers, and available statistics for questions about Australia during an internal evaluation,” Pusateri said in a statement.
Pusateri said OpenAI was supporting investigations and that its review was ongoing, adding it was committed “sharing what we learn as that work continues”.
